summary: Someone dying, someone buried: {the dying or dead} is dying or gone, and the player must say who is there, who stays, and who speaks.
realLife: One life: As a boy Grant lost his mother to cancer, did not go to her funeral and regrets it. His father later gave him a note she had written. His friend's mother became like a second mother to him, and her death years later moved him deeply. Another: About twenty years earlier she moved her ailing father into the family home and the household cared for him for seven years until he died. She says she did not think she had another choice and felt isolated while friends praised her. Her son valued the dignity of the death at home. Another: A daughter recorded a talk with her father in hospice at his New Jersey home, days before he died. Asked what he was proudest of, he said his children and family. He had paid off the home and died there with loved ones around him. Another: In 2007 his brother, with terminal cancer and in home hospice, moved from California to Utah near his adult children. Neighborhood women cleaned and furnished a small house before the family arrived at night. The brother died two days later with family around him.
